meta.origin: Hand-curated from the institutions' own published rate pages. There is no free public API for retail deposit rates: the FDIC API carries institution metadata and insurance status but not advertised APY, and NCUA publishes bulk quarterly files rather than a live feed.
meta.note: Offline snapshot at plausible levels for the stated date. Not a quote. Deposit rates move without notice — open the rate page on any row before you move money, and keep your own copy current in the user rates file (Settings -> Open my rates file).
meta.userFileShape: Same shape as this file: {"items": [ ... ]}. An item whose id matches one here REPLACES it; a new id is ADDED. Set dataAsOf on a row you refresh so the app trusts it more than the bundled snapshot.

items.name: Ally Bank Online Savings Account
items.accessNotes: Open online in about ten minutes with an SSN and a funding account; no minimum deposit, no monthly fee, six free transfers per cycle.
requirements: US resident with an SSN or ITIN
items.notes: Rate is set by the bank and can change any day, including the day after you fund the account.

items.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs Online Savings Account
items.accessNotes: Open online, no minimum; link an external account and pull funds in. Deposits sit at Goldman Sachs Bank USA, not at the broker-dealer.
items.notes: Marcus has historically offered a small rate boost through partner referral links; the base rate is what is shown here.

items.name: American Express High Yield Savings Account
items.accessNotes: Open online; no minimum and no monthly fee. Transfers are ACH only — there is no debit card and no branch network.
items.notes: No ATM access at all, so this is a place to park money rather than to spend from.

items.name: Discover Online Savings Account
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; fund by ACH, wire, or direct deposit.
items.notes: Discover Bank is now part of Capital One; product terms have so far been unchanged but are worth re-checking.

items.name: Capital One 360 Performance Savings
items.accessNotes: Open online or in a Capital One Cafe; no minimum, and unlike most online banks there is branch and ATM access.
items.notes: One rate for all balances — Capital One dropped the old tiered 360 Savings pricing, which is why the legacy 360 Savings account pays far less.

items.name: Synchrony Bank High Yield Savings
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; includes an optional ATM card, which is unusual for a high-yield savings account.
items.notes: Synchrony is a credit-card bank funding its card book with deposits, which is why it tends to sit near the top of the rate tables.

items.name: Barclays Online Savings Account
items.accessNotes: Open online; ACH transfers only, no ATM card, no branches.
items.notes: Deposits are at Barclays Bank Delaware, a separately capitalised US bank, not at the UK parent.

items.name: SoFi Checking and Savings
items.accessNotes: Open online; the headline rate only applies once qualifying direct deposit is running, so budget a pay cycle before you actually earn it.
requirements: Requires qualifying direct deposit to earn the top rate — without it the account pays roughly 1%
Rate applies to both the checking and savings balance
items.notes: SoFi sweeps balances to a network of partner banks, which raises the aggregate FDIC limit well above $250k but makes coverage depend on the current program bank list.

items.name: Wealthfront Cash Account
items.accessNotes: Open a Wealthfront brokerage account online, $1 minimum; money is swept to partner banks, and same-day withdrawals are capped.
items.notes: This is a brokerage sweep, not a bank account. FDIC coverage is pass-through from the program banks and only exists once the cash actually lands at one of them; the aggregate limit is far above $250k but depends on the current bank list.

items.name: Betterment Cash Reserve
items.accessNotes: Open through the Betterment app; no minimum, no fee on Cash Reserve, transfers settle in one to two business days.
items.notes: Betterment has repeatedly run a boosted rate for new customers for their first few months; the number here is the ongoing base rate, which is the one that matters after the boost lapses. Cash is swept to program banks, so FDIC coverage is pass-through.

items.name: Bask Bank Interest Savings Account
items.accessNotes: Open online; ACH only, no ATM card. Bask also offers an account that pays American Airlines miles instead of interest — that is a different product and usually a worse deal.
items.notes: Bask is the direct-bank brand of Texas Capital Bank; FDIC insurance is shared with any other Texas Capital deposits you hold.

items.name: UFB Direct Savings
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; includes an ATM card.
items.notes: UFB has a long habit of launching a freshly-named savings product at a top rate and quietly leaving existing customers on the old, lower one. Check which product name your account is actually on, not the one on the website.

items.name: EverBank Performance Savings
items.accessNotes: Open online; no minimum, no monthly fee.
items.notes: EverBank commits publicly to keeping existing customers on the same rate as new ones, which is the opposite of the usual online-bank practice.

items.name: Openbank by Santander High Yield Savings
requirements: Promotional intro APY — Openbank has marketed its headline rate as an introductory offer, so confirm the current terms and what it reverts to
Requires a minimum opening deposit and, in some offers, a recurring direct deposit to keep the promotional tier
items.accessNotes: Open through the Openbank app; funding minimum applies and the top tier has historically required keeping a direct deposit running.
items.notes: Santander's US direct bank. A promotional rate is a marketing expense with an end date — assume it reverts to something ordinary and check what the revert rate is before you move a large balance.

items.name: Varo Bank Savings Account
requirements: Bonus rate tier: requires qualifying direct deposits each month and a positive daily balance
Top rate applies only to the first $5,000 — the rest earns the base rate, roughly half as much
items.accessNotes: Open through the Varo app with a Varo checking account attached; the direct deposit test is measured monthly, so a missed month drops you to the base rate.
items.notes: The blended yield on a large balance is nowhere near the headline. On $50,000 the effective rate is closer to the base tier than to 5%.

items.name: DCU Primary Savings
requirements: Credit union membership required — join via a participating employer, association, or an eligible community
Top rate applies only to the first $1,000; the balance above it earns a small fraction of that
items.accessNotes: Join DCU online (membership is broad through partner organisations), keep $5 in the share account, then fund Primary Savings.
items.notes: A genuinely high rate on a genuinely tiny balance. Worth $60 a year, not a place to put a house deposit.

items.name: Vanguard Cash Plus Account
items.accessNotes: Open inside an existing Vanguard account; balances sweep to partner banks and can be moved into Vanguard funds without leaving the platform.
items.notes: Bank sweep, so FDIC-insured across several program banks — a different product from Vanguard's money market funds, which are not insured but usually yield a little more.

items.name: Fidelity Cash Management Account (FDIC bank sweep)
items.accessNotes: Open online; free ATM withdrawals worldwide with fee reimbursement, which is the real reason to hold one.
items.notes: Listed because the contrast matters: the FDIC sweep pays far less than SPAXX sitting in the same account. If you hold a Fidelity CMA, the cash usually belongs in the money market fund, not the sweep.

items.name: Fidelity Government Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: The default core position in most Fidelity brokerage accounts — cash you deposit is already in it, and it sells automatically to settle trades.
items.notes: Holds government repo as well as Treasuries, so the state-tax-exempt share is usually well under half. Quoted as the 7-day SEC yield, which is net of the expense ratio.

items.name: Fidelity Treasury Only Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: Buy as a normal mutual fund position inside a Fidelity account; it is not a core sweep option, so you have to place the trade yourself.
items.notes: Holds Treasuries directly and avoids repo, which is what makes most of the income state-tax-exempt. The exempt share is set each January for the prior year and has run above 90% but is not guaranteed.

items.name: Fidelity Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: Buy as a fund position in a Fidelity brokerage account; usable as a core position in some account types.
items.notes: A prime fund: it holds commercial paper and CDs, not just government paper. That is where the extra few basis points come from, and it is also why prime funds can gate or float in a real liquidity crisis.

items.name: Fidelity Money Market Fund Premium Class
items.accessNotes: Same portfolio as SPRXX at a lower fee, but it takes $100,000 to open the position ($10,000 in retirement accounts).
items.notes: The yield edge over SPRXX is just the class fee difference. If your balance drops below the minimum Fidelity can convert you back to the retail class.

items.name: Vanguard Federal Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: The settlement fund for every Vanguard brokerage account, so cash sits here by default; $3,000 minimum on a standalone purchase.
items.notes: An 11 basis point expense ratio is why this fund keeps beating most bank savings accounts. Government repo is a large share of the portfolio, so only part of the income is state-tax-exempt.

items.name: Vanguard Treasury Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: Buy as a fund inside a Vanguard brokerage account; $3,000 minimum, settles T+1.
items.notes: Almost entirely T-bills, so the state-exempt share has run very high — but Vanguard has used repo here in past years and the exempt percentage is published after the fact, not promised in advance. In a high-tax state this is often the best after-tax cash option on the list.

items.name: Vanguard Cash Reserves Federal Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: Buy as a fund position; $3,000 minimum. Cannot be used as the brokerage settlement fund, so you place the trade yourself.
items.notes: Nearly the same portfolio as VMFXX at a nearly identical fee; the yield difference between them is noise.

items.name: Vanguard Municipal Money Market Fund
items.accessNotes: Buy as a fund position in a Vanguard account; $3,000 minimum.
items.notes: The headline yield looks poor until you tax it. Federally exempt income at a 37% bracket makes 2.35% worth about 3.73% pre-tax — the app's after-tax ranking is where this row earns its place. Muni money market yields are seasonal and swing more than taxable ones.

items.name: Schwab Value Advantage Money Fund - Investor Shares
items.accessNotes: Buy as a fund position in a Schwab account. Schwab does not sweep to it automatically — uninvested cash sits in a bank sweep paying near nothing, so this trade has to be placed by hand.
items.notes: A prime fund holding commercial paper and CDs. The gap between this and Schwab's default cash sweep is the single largest avoidable yield giveaway on this list.

items.name: Schwab U.S. Treasury Money Fund - Investor Shares
items.accessNotes: Buy as a fund position in a Schwab account; no minimum, T+1 settlement.
items.notes: Treasury-only portfolio, so most of the income is state-tax-exempt — the exact share is published annually and varies. The 0.34% fee is why it trails Vanguard's Treasury fund.

items.name: Synchrony Bank 3 Month CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; rate is locked at funding and the CD auto-renews unless you act during the 10-day grace period.
items.notes: On a 3-month CD the early withdrawal penalty is the entire term's interest, so treat this as genuinely locked money.

items.name: Ally Bank 6 Month High Yield CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; Ally's Ten Day Best Rate guarantee gives you the best rate it offers in the ten days after you fund.
items.notes: Ally's penalty schedule is one of the mildest in the market — 60 days of interest on terms of 24 months or less.

items.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs 6 Month High-Yield CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with $500; you have 10 days after opening to fund it and the rate is guaranteed over that window.
items.notes: Auto-renews at whatever the rate is on the maturity date. Set a calendar reminder for the grace period.

items.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs 9 Month High-Yield CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with $500 minimum.
items.notes: Odd terms like 9 and 13 months are where banks put their promotional pricing, which is why this can beat the 1-year.

items.name: Capital One 360 12 Month CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; choose monthly, annual, or at-maturity interest payout when you open it.
items.notes: Compare against the 1-year Treasury before locking: a Treasury of the same maturity is state-tax-free and can be sold any day.

items.name: Alliant Credit Union 12 Month Certificate
requirements: Credit union membership required — anyone can qualify by joining Foster Care to Success, and Alliant pays the $5 fee
items.accessNotes: Join online in one sitting (eligibility through the charity route is open to anyone), then open the certificate inside online banking.
items.notes: NCUA insurance is the credit union equivalent of FDIC and is backed the same way, up to $250,000 per owner per institution.

items.name: Navy Federal 12 Month Standard Certificate
requirements: Membership limited to active duty, veterans, DoD civilians, and their family members
items.accessNotes: Eligibility is checked at join time and cannot be bought into; if you qualify, open the certificate in online banking.
items.notes: Navy Federal runs special certificate promotions for members several times a year that beat the standard rate shown here.

items.name: Discover Bank 18 Month CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; interest can be paid out monthly or compounded to maturity.
items.notes: Six months of interest on an 18-month CD wipes out a third of the total return if you break it early.

items.name: PenFed 18 Month Money Market Certificate
items.earlyExitPenalty: Up to 30% of the dividends the certificate would have earned over its full term
requirements: Credit union membership required — PenFed membership is open to anyone who opens a savings account
items.accessNotes: Join online with a $5 savings account, then open the certificate; there is no employer or military test.
items.notes: PenFed's penalty is calculated on the dividends the full term would have earned, not on days elapsed, so breaking one early is unusually expensive.

items.name: Synchrony Bank 24 Month CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum.
items.notes: The 2-year point is where the curve is flattest right now — you are locking two years of rate risk for less than the 9-month CD pays.

items.name: Ally Bank 3 Year High Yield CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum.
items.notes: 90 days of interest on a 3-year term makes this one of the cheapest long CDs to break — that optionality is worth real basis points if rates rise.

items.name: Discover Bank 36 Month CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum.
items.notes: Locking three years below the 3-month rate is a bet that rates fall further. That bet may be right, but name it before you make it.

items.name: Barclays 60 Month Online CD
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; interest is credited monthly and can be transferred out.
items.notes: Five years of insured, contractually fixed income. The risk here is not credit, it is that you are still holding 3.5% in year four.

items.name: Navy Federal 5 Year Standard Certificate
requirements: Membership limited to active duty, veterans, DoD civilians, and their family members
items.accessNotes: Open in online banking once membership is established; dividends can be paid monthly to a share account.
items.notes: Credit unions usually pay more than banks at the long end because they have no shareholders to pay first.

items.name: Ally Bank 11 Month No Penalty CD
requirements: Withdrawal must be the full balance — no partial withdrawals
Locked for the first 6 days after funding
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; after six days you can close it and take principal plus all interest earned, any day, for any reason.
items.notes: The genuinely useful product on this list: a rate close to a term CD with an option to walk away free. If rates rise you break it and re-open at the new rate; if they fall you keep the old one.

items.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs 13 Month No-Penalty CD
requirements: Withdrawal must be the full balance
Locked for the first 7 days after funding
items.accessNotes: Open online with $500; withdraw the full balance any time after the first week with no penalty.
items.notes: Marcus also offers 7 and 20 month no-penalty terms; the 13 month usually prices best.

items.name: Synchrony Bank 11 Month No-Penalty CD
requirements: Withdrawal must be the full balance
Locked for the first 6 days after funding
items.accessNotes: Open online with no minimum; full balance withdrawable without penalty after the first six days.
items.notes: Compare the give-up against Synchrony's own savings rate — if a no-penalty CD pays less than the bank's liquid savings account, it is strictly worse.
